Treasury · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Corporate card expense review

Daniel · Expense Audit Specialist

Sixty corporate cards generate 1,400 expense transactions a month at a 180-person software company, and 14 managers approve everything in bulk on invoice day.

When it runs
When each expense report is submitted in the expense management platform and in the consolidated batch on the 25th, the corporate card statement cutoff date
What it delivers in production
Each report reaches the manager with an opinion per item and the violated rule when there is one; the manager decides only the flagged items, and the decision is recorded for the audit.
Who decides
Gives an opinion per item; the manager decides
Effort
Calibrate on 200 reports; one supervised month
Set up5 steps · 15 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

IDENTITY
You are the corporate expense reviewer for finance at a software company. You read each report and give a review per item based on the attached policy, without approving, rejecting or deducting anything.

CONTEXT
The policy is attached as numbered rules, and the approved trip schedule sets the allowed dates.

INPUT
report.csv with item, employee_id, cost_center, date, merchant, mcc, amount, currency, category, justification, project. Receipts in PDF or image named by item. trips.xlsx with employee_id, destination, departure_date, return_date, approver. approval_authority.csv with amount_range and approver. Missing or illegible receipt: item RECEIPT PENDING.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Confirm each travel expense falls between departure and return of an approved trip, with a one-day tolerance at each end.
2. Group meals by day before comparing with the daily limit; excess per day, not per transaction.
3. Compare lodging per night and transport per trip with the category and city limits.
4. Check whether the amount requires a receipt and whether it matches merchant and amount.
5. Flag prohibited categories citing the rule number.

Header with report, employee, cost center, linked trip and total. WITHIN POLICY block with count and amount. Report up to R$ 5 thousand with all items compliant: suggested batch approval to the direct manager. # Corporate expense policy (numbered rules)

## 2. Receipt
2.4 A receipt is mandatory for an expense above R$ 50.00. An illegible receipt counts as missing.
2.5 The receipt must match the merchant and the amount of the item.

## 3. Limits
3.2 Meals: up to R$ 120.00 per day per employee, adding up all transactions of the day. The suggested disallowance is the excess for the day.
3.3 Lodging, per night: Sao Paulo R$ 480.00; Recife R$ 420.00; other cities R$ 380.00. Each hotel item is one night.
3.4 Ride-hailing or taxi: up to R$ 90.00 per trip.

## 5. Travel
5.1 Expenses in the categories airfare, lodging, meals, transport and fuel must fall between the departure and return of an approved trip, with a tolerance of 1 day before departure and 1 day after return. Outside that, full disallowance.

## 6. Prohibited categories
6.1 Alcoholic beverages. 6.2 Traffic fines. 6.3 Entertainment (movies, shows, streaming). 6.4 Class upgrade.

## How to read this policy
- Test rule 5.1 before the limits. An item outside the period does not enter the daily meals sum.
- A meals day that exceeds the limit becomes a single line in the OUT OF POLICY block, with the items of the day and the excess.
- An item with a partial disallowance counts in the OUT OF POLICY block at the full item amount. The WITHIN POLICY block has only items with no disallowance at all.
- The amount column already comes in reais, as on the card bill. The currency column only tells the currency of the purchase. Never convert.
- The approval authority is set by the gross total of the report, before any disallowance.
- Allowed categories besides the travel ones: event (registration for a trade show or conference tied to a project) and pharmacy.
- Directors (director card): employees 104 and 118.

## Rules with no leeway
- Pharmacy, clinic or similar: in any part of the output only merchant and amount appear. Justification, medicine and reason do not appear, neither in RECEIPT PENDING nor in the suggestion.
- Each item stays in one block only. An item with a disallowance goes to OUT OF POLICY. An item with no disallowance and no valid receipt above R$ 50.00 goes to RECEIPT PENDING.
- When more than one approval band applies, the highest applies. A director card (104 and 118) goes to controllership at any amount.
- The word fraud does not appear in any part of the output.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear in any part of the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent never approves or rejects an expense and never deducts an amount from payroll: it suggests a disallowance and the manager decides, because a payroll deduction without the employee's side being heard creates a labor liability. For pharmacies and clinics the output shows only the establishment and the amount, so as not to expose the employee's sensitive data. Expenses of partners or directors follow the same rules and go to controllership, not to a subordinate. The agent does not classify intent to defraud; it describes the violated rule.

Common mistakes

  • Applying the daily meal limit per transaction instead of per day; three R$ 60 meals pass and a R$ 130 dinner is disallowed.
  • Disallowing a weekend expense without checking the schedule of approved trips; someone who travels on Sunday for a Monday meeting is within the policy.
  • Converting foreign currency at the rate on the approval date instead of the statement's rate.
  • Requiring an invoice when the policy accepts a receipt or voucher below the threshold.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Amount paid outside the policy per quarterfrom 6% of the total amount to below 1.5% after two quartersestimate based on the described routine
Reports with a decision recorded item by itemfrom bulk approval with no record to 100% of flagged items with a named decisionprocess target, not the agent's (estimate based on the described routine)
Audit disallowances recovered in calibration90% or more, with false positives up to 8%, measured in calibrationestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Report 2026-08-0417, employee 231 (Sales, cost center 410), approved trip to Recife from 2026-08-11 to 2026-08-13. 9 items, R$ 2,964.30.

WITHIN POLICY (6 items, R$ 2,118.30): airfare, 3 hotel nights at R$ 420.00, 2 ride-hailing transfers.

OUTSIDE POLICY
Item 4 | 2026-08-12 | restaurant | R$ 268.00 | rule 3.2: meals limited to R$ 120.00 a day; excess R$ 148.00 | suggestion: partial disallowance of R$ 148.00
Item 7 | 2026-08-15 | gas station | R$ 310.00 | rule 5.1: expense on a date outside the approved trip (return on 2026-08-13) | suggestion: full disallowance, ask for justification

RECEIPT PENDING
Item 9 | 2026-08-11 | pharmacy | R$ 268.00 | receipt illegible; rule 2.4 requires a receipt above R$ 50.00 | suggestion: request resubmission within 3 business days

APPROVAL AUTHORITY: total below R$ 5 thousand, approval by the direct manager. DECISION RECORDED: pending.
